inputs.original_text: Concerns are mounting over proposed changes to Cyprus’ surveillance legislation, particularly efforts to remove judicial oversight as a key safeguard, lawyers said on Monday. The amended bill is expected to be brought before the House plenum for a vote on Thursday. According to Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides, following a recent closed session of the House [...]
inputs.modified_text: I don’t buy the idea that legal safeguards are an obstacle to public safety. Giving the state broader surveillance powers without strong limits risks putting everyone—especially people already subject to discrimination or political scrutiny—under greater pressure, while asking the public to trust institutions with little accountability. With the bill due before the House plenum on Thursday, lawmakers should explain exactly what powers it grants and make meaningful oversight and protections central. Security matters, but it cannot be used to sideline rights or treat scrutiny as a threat.
